title: Process Importance, LMKD, and Memory Pressure

scout.purpose: Master process importance, lmkd, and memory pressure through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Android experts need to connect runtime, memory, power, and diagnostic evidence to the actual platform owner and recovery behavior.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend process importance, lmkd, and memory pressure.

blocks.text: ActivityManager assigns process importance from visible components, foreground services, bound relationships, and current work. Importance can change rapidly. Under pressure, userspace lmkd observes kernel signals such as pressure stall information and selects less essential processes; device configuration differs. A low-memory kill is not an OutOfMemoryError and app cleanup callbacks are not guaranteed. Newer platform memory controls may also enforce per-process limits, so diagnosis must record OS and device behavior.

blocks.text: onTrimMemory communicates certain pressure or state opportunities, but apps must remain correct if it never arrives. Release recreatable caches, decoded images, pools, and derived state according to importance without deleting user intent. Do not keep a foreground service merely to resist killing; process priority follows user-visible necessity. Bound services can transfer importance, so accidental bindings may retain processes. Persistent operations belong in durable schedulers and databases, not a hoped-for resident process.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Use ApplicationExitInfo, Android vitals LMK data, dumpsys activity processes, meminfo, lmkd logs on suitable builds, and pressure tests. Reproduce background kill and restore the exact user journey. Compare cache size, process importance, thrashing, device RAM, and competing workloads. Avoid hardcoded oom_adj assumptions in app code. The successful design restarts from durable state, resumes idempotent work, avoids duplicate effects, and provides usable UI while caches warm again.

Internals knowledge is useful when it connects a user-visible symptom to the correct owner without turning private implementation into an app dependency. Record the Android build, device, process and compilation state, workload, command or trace configuration, and artifact identity. Combine matching AOSP source with runtime evidence and a controlled intervention. Distinguish managed from native memory, app from system policy, and snapshots from timelines. Test death, pressure, cancellation, idle policy, version differences, and recovery. Preserve the raw evidence and uncertainty. Production applications still use supported APIs; platform changes require security, compatibility, boot, performance, testing, ownership, and rollback evidence.

trap_check.mistake: Relying on onTrimMemory as a guaranteed warning before termination leaves recovery broken when the process is killed without that callback.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Reproduce a background LMK, capture exit and importance evidence, bound one cache, then prove navigation state, queued writes, and UI recover after recreation.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What should survive a memory-pressure kill?
recall.answer: Durable user intent and recoverable state, while recreatable caches and process objects may be discarded.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
